value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across SCE's entire distribution territory, which includes Thousand Oaks/Ventura County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: SolarAPP+ approval (obtained via the SolarAPP+ website)
City of Thousand Oaks TO/24 online permit application, with SolarAPP+ approval submitted and permit fees paid, to receive the City-issued State Solar Permit

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own Solar PV Systems page: any SolarAPP+ web-based approval is not itself a construction permit until applied for and submitted through TO/24 and fees are paid, at which point the City issues the State Solar Permit.

value: Inspections can only be scheduled through the city's TO/24 online portal

value.notes: The City's own Solar PV Systems page states the 'Pre-Approved OR Preauthorized Solar Inspection Permit' (SolarApp+ permit type) 'is an express permit that allows instant permit issuance for compliant systems to licensed contractors installing on residential properties.'

value.program_or_pathway: SolarAPP+ / State Solar Permit (roof-mounted residential only)
other_conditions: SolarAPP+/State Solar Permit is for roof-mounted solar on residential properties only, up to 38.4kW AC; ballasted, ground-mounted, and carport/parking-shade systems require a Standard Permit regardless of size
Only California-licensed B, C-10, or C-46 contractors may apply via SolarAPP+
The State Solar Permit is issued to the specific licensed contractor identified in the SolarAPP+ application and is non-transferable

The City's Municipal Code separately requires all roofs and solar systems to be fire-rated Class A (including the racking system) per UL1703 as locally amended, per Sections 8-1.14, 8-1.25, and 8-7.06
